learn.hook: A tiny neem seedling grows into a huge tree without eating a single meal. Where does all that food come from?
points: Green plants make their own food. This process is called photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using sunlight and the green pigment chlorophyll.
Leaves are the food factories of the plant. Carbon dioxide enters and oxygen leaves through tiny pores called stomata.
The glucose made is used for energy and growth, and extra food is stored as starch.
Iodine solution turns blue-black when it touches starch, so it can show which leaves made food. (Leaf testing involves hot alcohol, so it is done only by a teacher.)

example.q: One potted plant is kept in sunlight and an identical one in a dark cupboard for two days. A teacher tests a leaf from each with iodine. Which turns blue-black and why?
steps: Photosynthesis needs sunlight.
Only the plant in sunlight could make food and store it as starch.
Iodine turns blue-black where starch is present.
example.answer: The leaf from the plant in sunlight turns blue-black, because only it made starch by photosynthesis.

learn.reallife: Almost all the food we eat, from rice and wheat to mangoes and dal, comes from plants that made it by photosynthesis. Plants also release the oxygen we breathe.

games.title: What does photosynthesis use, and what does it make?

items.text: The green pigment in leaves is called ___.
Tiny pores on leaves are called ___.
Iodine turns ___ when it meets starch.

quiz.q: What is the main raw material that plants take from the air for photosynthesis?
quiz.explain: Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air through stomata and water from the soil.
steps: Photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen.
Carbon dioxide comes from the air; water comes from the soil.
So the raw material taken from the air is carbon dioxide.
Answer: Carbon dioxide
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants take in oxygen for making food

quiz.q: Which gas is given out during photosynthesis?
quiz.explain: Photosynthesis releases oxygen into the air, which animals and humans breathe.
steps: Photosynthesis gives out oxygen.
Animals and humans breathe this oxygen.
So oxygen is given out.
Answer: Oxygen
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the gas taken in and the gas given out

quiz.q: Why are leaves called the food factories of a plant?
quiz.explain: Leaves have chlorophyll and get sunlight, so most food is made in them.
steps: Leaves have chlorophyll and get sunlight.
They make most of the plant's food by photosynthesis.
So leaves are called food factories.
Answer: They make food by photosynthesis
quiz.mistake: Thinks roots make the plant's food

quiz.q: What is the role of chlorophyll?
quiz.explain: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that traps the Sun's energy for making food.
steps: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in leaves.
It captures the energy of sunlight for making food.
So it captures energy from sunlight.
Answer: It captures energy from sunlight
quiz.mistake: Does not know the job of chlorophyll

quiz.q: In what form do plants store extra food?
quiz.explain: Glucose is changed into starch for storage, for example in potatoes and grains.
steps: Glucose made in photosynthesis is used for energy and growth.
Extra food is stored as starch.
So plants store food as starch.
Answer: Starch
quiz.mistake: Confuses the stored food with the raw materials

quiz.q: Which test shows the presence of starch in a leaf?
quiz.explain: Iodine gives a blue-black colour with starch.
steps: Iodine solution turns blue-black with starch.
So the test is: the leaf turns blue-black with iodine.
Answer: It turns blue-black with iodine
quiz.mistake: Mixes up different chemical tests

quiz.q: A croton leaf has green and yellow patches. After a starch test, only the green parts turn blue-black. Why?
options: Yellow parts get no sunlight at all
Yellow parts have too much starch
Iodine does not work on yellow
Only the green parts have chlorophyll to make food
quiz.explain: Photosynthesis happens only where chlorophyll is present, so starch forms only in the green parts.
steps: Photosynthesis needs chlorophyll.
Only the green parts have chlorophyll, so only they make starch.
So only the green parts turn blue-black.
Answer: Only the green parts have chlorophyll to make food
quiz.mistake: Does not see that chlorophyll is needed

quiz.q: Through which part do carbon dioxide and oxygen enter and leave a leaf?
quiz.explain: Stomata are tiny openings, mostly on the underside of leaves, that let gases in and out.
steps: Leaves have tiny pores called stomata.
Carbon dioxide enters and oxygen leaves through them.
So the answer is stomata.
Answer: Stomata
quiz.mistake: Thinks gases enter through the roots

teach.ask: Gappu eats seeds to get energy. But a mango tree never eats! How does a plant get its food?
teach.praise: Tweet! Leaves use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food. Mango trees are master chefs!
teach.nudge: What do plants need from the air and the soil to make food?

revise.summary: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis: carbon dioxide and water form glucose and oxygen using sunlight and chlorophyll. Leaves are the food factories, and extra food is stored as starch.
focus: Word equation and conditions for photosynthesis
Role of chlorophyll, sunlight and stomata
remember: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (sunlight, chlorophyll)
Stomata let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out
Extra food is stored as starch
traps: Plants take in carbon dioxide, not oxygen, for photosynthesis.
Yellow parts of a croton leaf have no chlorophyll, so no starch.
Leaf testing uses hot alcohol: only a teacher should do it.

learn.hook: Water climbs all the way to the top of a tall coconut tree without any pump. How does it get up there?
points: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil, mainly through tiny root hairs.
Xylem is a set of tubes that carries water and minerals from the roots up to the stem, leaves and flowers.
Phloem is another set of tubes that carries food made in the leaves to all parts of the plant.
Plants lose water as vapour through stomata. This is called transpiration.
Transpiration creates a pull that helps draw water up through the xylem. It also cools the plant.

example.q: A white flower with its stem kept in water with a few drops of red ink turns pinkish after a few hours. What does this show?
steps: The coloured water was taken up by the stem.
It travelled upwards to the petals.
Water moves up through the xylem tubes.
example.answer: Water travels up the stem through the xylem to the flower.

learn.reallife: Gardeners water the soil near the roots, not the leaves, because roots absorb water. On hot days, trees cool the air around them partly through transpiration.

games.title: Match the plant part to its transport job
The path of water in a plant
items: Out through stomata as water vapour

quiz.q: Which tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
quiz.explain: Xylem tubes carry water and dissolved minerals upwards.
steps: Xylem tubes carry water and minerals.
They carry them from the roots up to the leaves.
So the answer is xylem.
Answer: Xylem
quiz.mistake: Mixes up xylem and phloem

quiz.q: Which tissue carries food from the leaves to other parts of the plant?
quiz.explain: Phloem carries the food made in leaves to the stem, roots, fruits and other parts.
steps: Phloem carries food made in the leaves.
It takes it to all parts of the plant.
So the answer is phloem.
Answer: Phloem
quiz.mistake: Mixes up phloem and xylem

quiz.q: What is transpiration?
options: Loss of water as vapour from the leaves
quiz.explain: Water evaporates through the stomata of leaves. This is transpiration.
steps: Plants lose water as vapour through stomata.
This loss is called transpiration.
So transpiration is loss of water as vapour from the leaves.
Answer: Loss of water as vapour from the leaves
quiz.mistake: Confuses transpiration with photosynthesis

quiz.q: How does transpiration help a plant?
options: It helps pull water up and cools the plant
It stops the roots from growing
quiz.explain: As water evaporates from leaves, more water is pulled up from the roots. Evaporation also cools the leaves.
steps: Water lost from leaves creates a pull up the xylem.
Evaporation also cools the plant.
So transpiration helps pull water up and cools the plant.
Answer: It helps pull water up and cools the plant
quiz.mistake: Thinks losing water can only be harmful

quiz.q: Through which part do plants mostly absorb water?
quiz.explain: Root hairs give a large surface area to absorb water and minerals from the soil.
steps: Roots absorb water mainly through tiny root hairs.
So plants mostly absorb water through root hairs.
Answer: Root hairs
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants drink water through their leaves

quiz.q: A stem is placed in water with red ink. Where will the red colour be seen inside the stem?
quiz.explain: The coloured water rises through the xylem, so these tubes look red when the stem is cut.
steps: Coloured water rises up the stem.
Water travels through the xylem.
So the red colour is seen in the xylem tubes.
Answer: In the xylem tubes
quiz.mistake: Does not know which tubes carry water

quiz.q: Why do plants need minerals from the soil?
quiz.explain: Minerals like nitrogen and potassium help plants grow and stay healthy.
steps: Roots absorb minerals from the soil along with water.
Minerals are needed for healthy growth.
So plants need minerals for healthy growth.
Answer: For healthy growth
quiz.mistake: Does not know why minerals are needed

quiz.q: On a hot, sunny day, a plant loses more water through its leaves. This is because:
quiz.explain: Heat speeds up evaporation, so more water escapes from the stomata.
steps: Transpiration is evaporation of water from leaves.
Heat speeds up evaporation.
So the plant loses more water because transpiration is faster in heat.
Answer: Transpiration is faster in heat
quiz.mistake: Does not link temperature with transpiration

teach.ask: Gappu poured water at the bottom of a sunflower plant. How does the water reach the top, and how does food travel around?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Xylem takes water up, phloem takes food around, and transpiration helps pull. Gappu's sunflower stands tall!
teach.nudge: Which tubes carry water upwards in a plant?

revise.summary: Roots absorb water and minerals through root hairs. Xylem carries water and minerals up; phloem carries food from the leaves to all parts. Transpiration is water loss from leaves, which pulls water up and cools the plant.
focus: Jobs of root hairs, xylem and phloem
remember: Xylem: water and minerals, roots → leaves
Transpiration = loss of water vapour through stomata
Transpiration pulls water up and cools the plant
traps: Don't mix up xylem (water) and phloem (food).
Transpiration is faster, not slower, on hot sunny days.

learn.hook: Plants make oxygen, so do they ever need oxygen themselves? Surprise: yes, all day and all night!
points: Like animals, plants respire: they break down food using oxygen to release energy, giving out carbon dioxide.
Every living part of a plant (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, seeds) respires, day and night.
Leaves take in air through stomata. Roots take oxygen from the air in the spaces between soil particles.
Over-watering fills these spaces with water, so roots cannot get enough air and the plant may die.
In daylight, photosynthesis makes more oxygen than the plant uses, so plants give out oxygen. At night, with no photosynthesis, plants only respire and give out carbon dioxide.

example.q: Sprouting moong seeds are kept in a closed flask. After a day, the air from the flask turns lime water milky, and the flask feels slightly warm. What is happening?
steps: Lime water turns milky with carbon dioxide.
The sprouting seeds are alive and respiring.
Respiration gives out carbon dioxide and releases energy, some as heat.
example.answer: The germinating seeds are respiring, giving out carbon dioxide and heat.

learn.reallife: Mangrove trees in the Sundarbans grow in waterlogged mud, so some of their roots grow upwards out of the mud to take in air.

games.title: Plant respiration check
items: Plants respire all the time; at night there is no photosynthesis, so respiration is easier to notice.
Roots take oxygen from air spaces in the soil.
Water fills the air spaces in soil, so roots cannot get oxygen.
Germinating seeds give out carbon dioxide.
Sprouting seeds respire actively and release carbon dioxide.
Plants give out carbon dioxide at night.
At night there is no photosynthesis, so plants only respire and give out carbon dioxide.
Photosynthesis and respiration are the same process.
Photosynthesis makes food and gives out oxygen; respiration uses food and oxygen to release energy.

quiz.q: When do plants respire?
options: All the time, day and night
quiz.explain: All living cells need energy all the time, so plants respire both day and night.
steps: Every living part of a plant respires.
It respires day and night.
So plants respire all the time.
Answer: All the time, day and night
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants respire only at night

quiz.q: How do the roots of a plant get oxygen?
options: From air in the spaces between soil particles
From the leaves only, through the xylem
quiz.explain: Soil has tiny air spaces between particles, and roots take oxygen from there.
steps: Soil has air in the spaces between its particles.
Roots take oxygen from this air.
So roots get oxygen from the air spaces in the soil.
Answer: From air in the spaces between soil particles
quiz.mistake: Believes roots do not need oxygen

quiz.q: Why can a potted plant die if it is watered too much?
options: Water fills the air spaces and roots cannot get oxygen
quiz.explain: When the soil is waterlogged, roots cannot respire properly.
steps: Over-watering fills the air spaces in the soil with water.
Roots then cannot get enough oxygen to respire.
So the plant may die.
Answer: Water fills the air spaces and roots cannot get oxygen
quiz.mistake: Thinks more water is always better

quiz.q: What gas do germinating seeds give out?
quiz.explain: Sprouting seeds respire quickly and give out carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.
steps: Germinating seeds respire.
Respiration gives out carbon dioxide (turns lime water milky).
So the gas is carbon dioxide.
Answer: Carbon dioxide
quiz.mistake: Thinks plants and seeds always give out oxygen

quiz.q: During the day, why do plants give out oxygen even though they are also respiring?
options: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
They stop respiring in the day
quiz.explain: Both processes happen in daylight, but photosynthesis is usually faster, so extra oxygen is released.
steps: In daylight both photosynthesis and respiration happen.
Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than the plant uses.
So extra oxygen is given out.
Answer: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
quiz.mistake: Thinks respiration stops when photosynthesis starts

quiz.q: Which process uses oxygen and releases energy from food?
quiz.explain: Respiration breaks down food using oxygen to release energy.
steps: Respiration breaks down food using oxygen.
It releases energy.
So the answer is respiration.
Answer: Respiration
quiz.mistake: Mixes up respiration and photosynthesis

quiz.q: Why do some mangrove trees have roots growing upwards out of the mud?
options: To make food in sunlight like leaves
To take in air, because the mud is waterlogged
quiz.explain: Waterlogged mud has little air, so these special roots grow upward to take in oxygen.
steps: Mangroves grow in waterlogged mud with little air.
Their special roots grow upwards to take in air.
So the roots grow upwards to take in air.
Answer: To take in air, because the mud is waterlogged
quiz.mistake: Does not connect root shape with the need for oxygen

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT respire?
quiz.explain: All living parts of a plant respire. Only dead parts, like a dry fallen stick, do not.
steps: All living parts of a plant respire.
Roots, leaves and sprouting seeds are living.
A dry, dead stick is not living.
So the dead wooden stick does not respire.
Answer: A dry, dead wooden stick
quiz.mistake: Thinks only leaves respire

teach.ask: Gappu heard plants give out oxygen, so they must not need any oxygen. Is Gappu right?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Plants respire day and night just like Gappu. They need oxygen too!
teach.nudge: Do plants need oxygen at night as well as in the day?

revise.summary: Plants respire all the time, breaking down food with oxygen to release energy and give out carbon dioxide. Roots take oxygen from soil air spaces, so over-watering harms them.
focus: Respiration in all living plant parts, day and night
How leaves and roots get oxygen
Why over-watering harms plants; mangrove roots
Why plants give out oxygen in the day but carbon dioxide at night
remember: Roots get oxygen from air spaces between soil particles
Daytime: photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
Night: plants only respire and give out carbon dioxide
traps: Don't think plants respire only at night.
Photosynthesis and respiration are different processes.
Dead parts like a dry stick do not respire.
